clue.text: Spouted pan I used for dumplings

indicators.note: spouted means spoken out loud, so the words before it are heard rather than written

parts.note: to pan a show is to knock it, criticise it harshly; taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook uses a pan with a spout to make dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spouted' looks like a description of the pan but signals sound: KNOCK plus I, said out loud, matches the Italian word, pronounced 'nocky' by English speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian potato or semolina dumplings, usually served with a sauce.

clue.text: Is not Eric both endlessly confused and louder?

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the gathered letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: both endlessly means each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: the two words taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a man called Eric is both muddled and making more noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both endlessly' trims NOT to NO and ERIC to ERI; with IS these make ISNOERI, which 'confused' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier is the comparative of noisy, making more sound, which is what louder means.

clue.text: A crucial point made by angry coloniser in speech

parts.note: cross is a common word for angry or annoyed

indicators.note: in speech means the name is heard, not spelt, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was the British imperialist who colonised what became Rhodesia

explanation.surface: An irate colonial figure makes a vital point while giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes was a 19th-century British empire-builder in southern Africa; his surname sounds like ways for traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction where two routes meet is used figuratively for a decisive moment when a choice must be made.

clue.text: Apathy, sadly, about one Greek mathematician

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the single letter
sadly here means badly or poorly, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Indifference, regrettably, concerning a certain Greek mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges APATHY to HYPATA, and 'about' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypatia of Alexandria was a celebrated female scholar of mathematics and astronomy, killed in 415 AD.

clue.text: Company board laundered money for the Contras

indicators.note: laundered means washed or cleaned up, so the letters of the word are recast

explanation.surface: A company's directors launder money for Nicaraguan rebels, like the Iran-Contra affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The cordoba is the currency of Nicaragua, where the Contras were rebels in the 1980s.

clue.text: Army types (wrongly!) taking over Channel Islands, including Jersey?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: including means the island letters hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: a jersey is a knitted top

explanation.surface: Soldiers wrongly invade the Channel Islands, Jersey among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the island but is the garment. 'Army' is cryptic for many-armed, and '(wrongly!)' admits the plural is the disputed one, octopuses being correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures with eight arms are the most 'army' of types; the Latin-style plural is commonly considered incorrect.

clue.text: Committee follows Bob down a plank over muddy ground

indicators.note: follows means the committee word comes after the next piece

parts.note: to bob down quickly is to duck
a board is a committee that runs an organisation

explanation.surface: A committee member bobs down after another, who stands on a plank over mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A duckboard is a slatted wooden walkway laid across mud, as in the trenches.

clue.text: Singer Charles stops crooner behaving like an ass

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous American crooner
Ray Charles was the American soul singer

explanation.surface: Ray Charles silences a crooner who is making a fool of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's harsh call is a bray, so making that noise is acting like the animal.

clue.text: Evolutionary biologist flared up over barrier supported by American church

indicators.note: over means in this down clue the rearranged word sits above the next piece
supported by means in a down answer the wall rests on the pieces below
up means stirred or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: An evolutionary scientist loses his temper at a barrier propped up by a US church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flared up' reads as one phrase but 'up' alone rearranges FLARED to ALFRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Russel Wallace devised a theory of natural selection independently of Darwin.

clue.text: A lot of tar without a storage unit

indicators.note: without means the following letter is dropped
a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Much tar is kept without a proper storage facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts SAILOR to SAILO, and 'without a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain or fodder on a farm.

clue.text: Italian banker settled in, keeping the company of US senator?

parts.note: the Po is an Italian river; a river has banks
a bird that has settled has lit or alighted

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the word in surrounds the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
the Company is a nickname for the CIA

explanation.surface: An Italian financier settles in and keeps company with an American senator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river, here the Po.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is an example of an elected lawmaker, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Portion of lentils I tasted in Sovetsk once

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sampling a little of the lentils while in a Russian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', but that is a link word: the town's former name is defined by 'Sovetsk once' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian town of Sovetsk in Kaliningrad was called by its German name, also a cheese, before 1946.

clue.text: Country inn hosted by old crock

indicators.note: hosted by means the inn is held inside the next word

parts.note: an old crock is a relic, something worn out and outdated
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A country inn run by an elderly wreck of a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation governed without a monarch.

clue.text: Island dryad swimming around nude in river

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters enclose the next piece
swimming means moving about, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: raw can mean naked, as in 'in the raw'

explanation.surface: A wood nymph swims naked in a river around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nude' gives RAW as in 'in the raw'; the swimming nymph's letters wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irrawaddy is the main river of Myanmar (Burma).

clue.text: Ethiopian princess takes an Arabian camel when there's no trains

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: when there's no means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: the dromedary is the one-humped Arabian camel
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs trains

explanation.surface: A royal takes a camel because the trains aren't running.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was the daughter of the Ethiopian king Cepheus, rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Mark tailless animal with stripes

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the badger has distinctive black-and-white face stripes

explanation.surface: Mark a striped animal that has no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb or name; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or token that marks out its wearer.

clue.text: See 3
Put down work papers

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: An instruction to put down one's work papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a revolt or a people is to subjugate them harshly.

clue.text: Too fatigued to feud anew after consuming a horse, say

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the rearranged letters hold the next pieces
anew means made again in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone too exhausted to restart a quarrel after eating a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges TO FEUD into F...EDOUT, which takes in A and GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out, exhausted, means being too tired to do anything more.

clue.text: A look that could excite e.g. English lady

indicators.note: could excite means stir up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: e.g. and lady are taken as written; English gives E, its standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A glance that might stir an English lady's feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirtatious or amorous glance is a come-hither look of sexual interest.

clue.text: Retired singer had to cry at Dubai wedding?

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so in this down answer the word is written backwards

parts.note: Lulu is the Scottish pop singer
to have had a meal is to have ate it; ate means had

explanation.surface: A singer in retirement had to weep at a wedding in Dubai.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop star of 'Shout' fame. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A high trilling wail is a traditional sound of celebration at Arab weddings.

clue.text: Watchdog and old French horse lacking focus

indicators.note: lacking focus means the middle of the word is removed

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: A watchdog and an elderly French horse that can't concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ofsted is the UK schools inspectorate. 'focus' means the centre: one E of the middle EE goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The schools inspectorate is a regulatory body that monitors standards, the sense of watchdog.

clue.text: A bit of nudity in parody by university lecturer? Just a bit

indicators.note: in means that letter goes inside the parody word

parts.note: a spoof is a parody

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A university lecturer's parody includes a little nudity, but only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measured amount is a modest quantity, the sense of just a bit.

clue.text: A line of approach an archdeacon uses regularly

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: An archdeacon routinely adopts a particular approach.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way of tackling a problem, a figurative route toward something.

clue.text: Discontented cat shuns milk supplement

indicators.note: shuns means avoids, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: to milk something is to extract from it

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of its contents, losing the middle letter

explanation.surface: An unhappy cat refuses milk as a dietary supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' reduces CAT to CT, which 'shuns' removes from EXTRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added on beyond the usual, an addition or supplement.

clue.text: Container with unusually clear coating but without 3

indicators.note: coating means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged
without means the following letter is removed

parts.note: but can mean except, as in 'all but one'
3 points to the first word of 3 Down, an X-shaped mark, so it supplies X

explanation.surface: A container with an oddly clear coating, but lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns CLEAR into R...ACLE, and 'without 3' strips X from EXCEPT, giving ECEPT for the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any vessel or holder for receiving and containing things.

clue.text: A loathsome person is kicked in the ear

indicators.note: in the ear means as heard, so the word is replaced by one sounding alike

parts.note: to be toed is to be kicked with the toe

explanation.surface: A horrible man gets a kick in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A repulsive or contemptible person is called after the warty amphibian.

clue.text: Islamic State secures areas surrounded by water

parts.note: to land a deal or catch is to secure it

explanation.surface: A militant group takes territory bordered by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Islands are pieces of land with water on every side.

clue.text: Some people at times will form household communities

parts.note: men are some people
ages are long times or eras

explanation.surface: Some people sometimes set up communal households.
explanation.definitionFit: A menage is a domestic establishment, the people living together in one home.
